korea-university-isc-2027.about:
Korea University's International Summer Campus (ISC) is one of Asia's largest summer schools. Students take credit-bearing courses taught in English by faculty from KU and universities worldwide (business, economics, international relations, Korean studies, engineering, media and more) or study Korean language, and join cultural activities such as taekwondo classes, baseball games and museum trips.

The 2026 edition ran from 29 June with 4-week and 6-week tracks; applications ran 19 January – 15 May 2026. On-campus dormitories are available, and KU ISC announces alumni and other scholarships on its notice board.
highlights: Credit-bearing courses in English at a top Korean university
Korean language option and rich cultural programme
korea-university-isc-2027.eligibility: University students (and some recent graduates/high-school graduates, per ISC rules) from any country; courses in English, so good English is needed.
how_to_apply: Check the ISC site in January 2027 for the 2027 application
Choose your courses and programme length
Submit the online application and pay the application fee
Pay tuition by the registration due date and apply for a dormitory
korea-university-isc-2027.costs: Paid: tuition per credit/course plus optional dormitory (see the ISC 'Fees & Payment' page). Some scholarships for alumni and partners.

kotlin-heroes-episode-15.about:
Kotlin Heroes rounds are 2.5-hour algorithmic contests run on Codeforces with JetBrains, the creator of Kotlin. They introduce competitive programmers to Kotlin and reward top finishers with prizes such as cash and branded merchandise (see the round announcement).

A practice round opens a week earlier so newcomers can learn Kotlin syntax before the main event.
kotlin-heroes-episode-15.eligibility: Anyone with a Codeforces account; prize rules in the official announcement.
how_to_apply: Create a Codeforces account
Try the practice round (from 20 Nov)
Register for Episode 15 and compete on 27 Nov 2026, 14:35 UTC

la-hacks-2027.about:
LA Hacks 2027 is one of the largest student hackathons in California, held at UCLA's Pauley Pavilion and free to attend. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at UCLA, Pauley Pavilion in Los Angeles from 2027-04-16 to 2027-04-18. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Build a portfolio project in one weekend
la-hacks-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open https://lahacks.com/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
la-hacks-2027.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

lane-kirkland-scholarship-program-2027-2.about:
The Lane Kirkland Scholarship Program brings young professionals and leaders from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Moldova, Tajikistan, Ukraine and Uzbekistan to Poland for two semesters of non-degree study at partner universities in Warsaw, Kraków, Lublin and Wrocław. Fellows follow an individual programme, do a professional internship and write a final project they can use back home.

Fields include economics and management, public administration, law, sociology and social psychology, political science and international relations, development policy, environmental protection, security and crisis management. It suits civil servants, lawyers, entrepreneurs, NGO leaders, journalists and academic teachers who plan to return home and apply what they learn.

The competition is announced every December and the deadline is always 1 March; shortlisted candidates are interviewed in March–April and results come by the end of May. Studies can be in Polish or English (B2), but English-track candidates also need basic Polish (A1).
highlights: Two fully funded semesters at leading Polish universities
Includes a professional internship and a final project
Georgia is an eligible country; deadline 1 March every year
lane-kirkland-scholarship-program-2027-2.eligibility: Citizens and permanent residents of Georgia (or another listed country); Master's degree or equivalent; up to 40 years old; at least 2 years' professional experience; Polish or English at B2 (English-track candidates also need A1 Polish); no foreign scholarship over 6 months in the previous 2 years.
how_to_apply: Watch for the 2027/28 call in December 2026 on kirkland.edu.pl
Complete the online application form with a study/project plan (4,000–6,000 characters)
Send two reference letters (Polish, English or Russian) and a copy of your Master's diploma by email
Submit by 1 March 2027; shortlisted candidates are interviewed in March–April
lane-kirkland-scholarship-program-2027-2.costs: Scholarship covers study costs and living allowance in Poland for two semesters (see programme terms).

lfx-mentorship-2027.about:
LFX Mentorship is the Linux Foundation's programme for learning open-source development under a mentor. Projects from the Linux Foundation family (for example CNCF/Kubernetes, Hyperledger and others) post mentorships each term; mentees work on a defined project with weekly reviews.

Anyone aged 18 or over who has not already completed an LFX mentorship may apply. You build a profile, apply to up to three programmes per term, and mentors score applicants on skills fit and intent. Where a stipend is offered it varies by programme and country of residence, and is paid in instalments after evaluations.

Terms recur throughout the year (typically spring, summer and autumn), so new 2027 openings appear on the platform regularly.
highlights: Real mentorship on major open-source projects
lfx-mentorship-2027.eligibility: Anyone aged 18+ who has not previously completed an LFX mentorship and can commit consistent hours for the term.
how_to_apply: Create an LFX profile with skills, links and a short introduction.
Browse open programmes for the current term.
Apply to up to three programmes (tasks or cover letters as requested).
If matched, complete the term and the final evaluation.
lfx-mentorship-2027.costs: Free. Stipends vary by programme and country of residence.

liysf-2027.about:
Founded in 1959, LIYSF is a 14-day residential STEM forum held each July in London. Participants attend principal lectures from leading scientists (past speakers include Nobel laureates), specialist lectures, visits to research labs, universities and companies, and present their own projects at the Science Bazaar, all while living on a university campus with students from around 70 countries.

The 2027 forum runs 18–31 July in a hybrid format (on campus in London or online). It is a paid programme; some national organisations and schools sponsor delegates, so ask your national science body or school about nominations.
highlights: Lectures from world-leading scientists and visits to top labs
Present your own research at the Science Bazaar
liysf-2027.eligibility: Students aged 16–21 with a strong interest in science, from any country, with good English.
how_to_apply: Read the 2027 programme on liysf.org.uk
Click 'Apply now' and complete the online application
Ask your school or national science organisation whether they sponsor delegates
Pay the fee once accepted and arrange a UK visa if needed
liysf-2027.costs: Paid programme; the fee (published on the LIYSF site) covers accommodation, meals, lectures and visits. Travel to London and visas are extra. Some delegates are sponsored by schools or national bodies.

luimun-2026.about:
LUIMUN 2026 is organised by the Leading University Model United Nations Association (LUMUNA), founded in 2016, and marks its fifth international edition. It runs over four days, 23–26 December 2026, in Sylhet in north-east Bangladesh under the theme 'A World in Transition: Reimagining Global Cooperation, Advancing Human Progress, and Shaping Our Shared Future'.

Ten committees include the UN Security Council and the International Court of Justice, and the conference expects more than 400 delegates. It is open to school and university students from Bangladesh and abroad.

A good-value, four-day international conference for South Asian students looking to build MUN experience.
luimun-2026.eligibility: High-school and university students from Bangladesh and other countries. English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Open the LUIMUN 2026 site and read the committees and FAQ
Click Register Now and submit the delegate form
Pay the registration fee as instructed
Prepare position papers and attend 23–26 December
luimun-2026.costs: Registration fee shown in the official registration form; travel and accommodation are not included.

lumun-xxiii-2027.about:
LUMS Model United Nations (LUMUN) is a student-run conference at the Lahore University of Management Sciences that has brought together school, college and university delegates from across Pakistan for more than twenty years. LUMUN XXIII takes place on 4–7 January 2027 at LUMS, Lahore, with a programme of general, specialised and crisis committees chaired by experienced student officers.

Delegates can register as a delegation of 2–10 students from a school, college or university, or as private (individual) delegates; international delegates have their own fee band, and accommodation and socials can be booked during registration. Mandatory liability and code-of-conduct documents must be acknowledged before paying.

It is a large, competitive four-day conference and a strong choice for students in South Asia who want serious debate and a well-known name on their CV.
highlights: One of Pakistan's oldest and largest MUNs (23rd edition)
Delegation (2–10) or private-delegate registration; international fee band
lumun-xxiii-2027.eligibility: School, college (A-level/intermediate) and university students; delegates from outside Pakistan are welcome and pay the international rate. English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Read the committees on lumun.lums.edu.pk
Choose Delegation (2–10 delegates) or Private Delegate on the Register page
Fill in the form with preferences and accept the waiver and code of conduct
Pay the fee and upload proof of payment
Receive your allocation and prepare position papers
lumun-xxiii-2027.costs: Delegate fee depends on the early-bird/regular round and on whether you are a local or international delegate (shown in the registration form). Accommodation and social events are optional add-ons.

maastricht-summer-school-2027.about:
Maastricht Summer School (MSS), founded in 2012, offers short summer courses that complement Maastricht University's degree programmes, in Art & Culture, Business & Economics, Law & Politics, Science, Social Sciences and Lifelong Learning. Recent courses included Development Economics, Gender, Conflict and Peacebuilding, Digital Transformations in Public Health and Introduction to Data Analytics, taught in Maastricht's problem-based, small-group style.

Courses are aimed at undergraduate and graduate students and professionals, with a social programme in one of the Netherlands' most international student cities. The 2027 course list is being prepared and applications open in early 2027.
highlights: Problem-based learning in small international groups
Courses from economics and law to public health and data analytics
Social programme in a historic, very international city
maastricht-summer-school-2027.eligibility: Bachelor's or master's students and professionals, depending on the course; all nationalities. English proficiency required.
how_to_apply: Check maastrichtsummerschool.nl for the 2027 course list (early 2027)
Choose a course and check level, fee and deadline
Apply online with the requested documents
Book housing and arrange a visa if needed
maastricht-summer-school-2027.costs: Fees vary per course (listed on each course page once published); housing extra.

makeuc-2026.about:
MakeUC 2026 is a 24-hour hackathon hosted by IEEE at the University of Cincinnati. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at University of Cincinnati (IEEE) in Cincinnati from 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-08. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Build a portfolio project in one weekend
makeuc-2026.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open https://makeuc.io/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
makeuc-2026.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

makeuoft-2027.about:
MakeUofT 2027 is Canada's largest makeathon, focused on hardware projects. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at University of Toronto in Toronto from 2027-02-13 to 2027-02-14. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Build a portfolio project in one weekend
makeuoft-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open http://makeuoft.ca/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging

mamunc-iii-2026.about:
MAMUNC is a one-day Model UN hosted at Menlo-Atherton High School in the San Francisco Bay Area.

The conference runs 14 November 2026 at Menlo-Atherton High School, 555 Middlefield Rd, United States. It is open to middle and high school students. Working language: English.

Use 'Register Now!' on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
mamunc-iii-2026.eligibility: Open to middle and high school students. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Use 'Register Now!' on the official site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
mamunc-iii-2026.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

marihacks-2027.about:
MariHacks 2027 is a Montreal hackathon run by and for high-school and CEGEP students. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at Marianopolis College in Montreal from 2027-04-09 to 2027-04-10. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Build a portfolio project in one weekend
how_to_apply: Open https://www.marihacks.com/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
marihacks-2027.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

marimun-2027.about:
MariMUN is the Model UN conference of Marianopolis College in Montreal ('Defying passivity, leading with purpose'), with a delegate handbook and committee list on its site.

The conference runs 13–14 February 2027 at Marianopolis College, Montreal, Canada. It is open to high school and CEGEP students. Working language: English.

Registration is 'coming soon' on the official site; follow MariMUN's social media for the opening. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
marimun-2027.eligibility: Open to high school and CEGEP students. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Registration is 'coming soon' on the official site; follow MariMUN's social media for the opening.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
marimun-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

masschallenge-challenge-program-boston-2.about:
MassChallenge is a global, non-profit accelerator known for taking no equity from the startups it supports. Its Challenge Program for the 2026-2027 cycle pairs startups with corporate partners (for example MassMutual) who publish specific challenge statements, mainly in fintech, insurance, and healthcare and life sciences.

Selected startups work with partner teams and MassChallenge experts from February to June 2027, with required in-person events in Boston. It is aimed at pre-seed to Series A companies with a product that can be piloted; international applicants are accepted.

Applications opened on 19 October 2026 and close on 9 November 2026 through the MassChallenge application portal.
highlights: Pre-seed to Series A; international teams accepted
masschallenge-challenge-program-boston-2.eligibility: Startups from any country, pre-seed to Series A, able to attend required in-person events in Boston.
how_to_apply: Read the 2026-2027 challenge statements and pick the one that fits.
Register on the MassChallenge application portal.
Submit the application by 9 November 2026.
Take part in judging rounds if shortlisted.
masschallenge-challenge-program-boston-2.costs: No fee and no equity stated. Travel to Boston is at the startup's own cost.

mate-rov-world-championship-2027.about:
The MATE ROV Competition, supported by the US National Science Foundation and the Marine Technology Society, has classes from Scout and Navigator (beginners) through Ranger and Pioneer to Explorer (advanced, mostly university). Teams build an ROV, write technical documentation, give an engineering presentation and complete product demonstrations in a pool.

Teams qualify through regional contests held in the US and in many other countries; Ranger, Pioneer and Explorer winners advance to the World Championship.
highlights: Classes from beginner to university level
mate-rov-world-championship-2027.eligibility: Student teams from middle school to university, competing in the class matching their level; international teams enter through MATE regional contests.
how_to_apply: Pick your class and read the 2027 competition manual
Register your team on materovcompetition.org
Compete at a regional event (spring 2027)
Qualify for the World Championship
mate-rov-world-championship-2027.costs: Registration fees per team; ROV build and travel self-funded.

math-kangaroo-usa-2027.about:
Math Kangaroo is the US branch of the International Kangaroo competition, taken by millions of students in 90+ countries. It is a multiple-choice test of logical reasoning and problem solving, with separate levels for each grade pair.

The 2027 individual competition takes place in March 2027 at registered test centres across the US; all participants receive a commemorative gift for the 30th anniversary, and top scorers win awards and national rankings.
highlights: Part of the international Kangaroo (90+ countries)
math-kangaroo-usa-2027.eligibility: Students in grades K–12 in the United States (outside the US, enter your country's own Kangaroo organiser).
how_to_apply: Find a Math Kangaroo test centre near you on the website
Register and pay the fee online
Practise with past papers
Take the test in March 2027
math-kangaroo-usa-2027.costs: Registration fee per student (set by Math Kangaroo USA; see the registration page).

mathcounts-competition-series-2026-27.about:
MATHCOUNTS runs written and oral rounds (Sprint, Target, Team and the Countdown Round) for students in grades 6–8. Schools register, practise and run a school competition from November, then send up to 14 competitors to chapter contests in February 2027; winners advance to state contests in March and the RTX MATHCOUNTS National Competition on 9–10 May 2027.

It is the classic US pathway to later olympiad success (AMC, USAMO).
mathcounts-competition-series-2026-27.eligibility: Students in grades 6–8 at US schools (all 50 states and territories, plus US-affiliated schools per MATHCOUNTS rules).
how_to_apply: Ask a teacher/coach to register your school
Practise with MATHCOUNTS materials
Compete at your school, then chapter (Feb) and state (Mar)
mathcounts-competition-series-2026-27.costs: School registration fee (see MATHCOUNTS); no extra fees to advance to state.

mcm-icm-2027.about:
MCM (Mathematical Contest in Modeling) and ICM (Interdisciplinary Contest in Modeling) are run by COMAP. Tens of thousands of teams from around the world choose one of six problems (continuous, discrete, data insights, operations research, sustainability, policy) and have four days to build a model and write a solution paper.

Teams need a faculty advisor who registers them in advance. Results (Outstanding, Finalist, Meritorious, Honorable Mention) are well recognised by graduate programmes and employers in quantitative fields.
highlights: Teams of up to 3 with an advisor
Six problem types incl. policy and data
mcm-icm-2027.eligibility: College/university undergraduates and high-school students worldwide; teams of up to three registered by a faculty advisor at their institution.
how_to_apply: Find a faculty advisor at your school or university
Advisor registers the team on contest.comap.com and pays the fee before the contest
Download problems when the contest opens on 28 January
Submit your solution paper by the 1 February deadline
mcm-icm-2027.costs: Registration fee per team (paid by the advisor; see COMAP).

medforum-digital-smart-youth-work-cervia.about:
Digital and Innovative Smart Youth Work brings at least 30 youth workers from eight countries (Italy as host, Morocco, Czechia, Greece, Jordan, Lithuania, Romania and Türkiye) to Mare e Vita Village in Pinarella di Cervia, Italy, on 11–17 December 2026 (including two travel days). It is co-funded by the European Union.

Workshops, simulations, peer learning and group work cover digital tools in youth work, digital storytelling, gamification, virtual facilitation, online safety and AI in youth education. Each participant develops a mini project to apply at home; results feed an open-access digital toolkit and an alumni network.

This call, published by Med-Forum SD (Rabat), is for the four places of the Moroccan group. Applicants from the other partner countries should contact the partner organisation in their own country.
highlights: Practical digital-youth-work toolkit including AI and online safety
International group from Europe, North Africa and the Middle East
Travel (capped), shared room, three meals, insurance and materials covered
medforum-digital-smart-youth-work-cervia.eligibility: Youth workers, educators or youth leaders aged 18+ with Moroccan nationality or legal residence in Morocco (4 places), able to work in English, available 11–17 December 2026, with basic digital literacy. No previous experience required; a valid Schengen visa gives priority.
how_to_apply: Read the project page on the Med-Forum SD website.
Fill in the application form embedded on the page (Google Form) by 17 November 2026.
Make sure your passport and Schengen visa situation allow travel to Italy in December.
Only selected applicants are contacted.
medforum-digital-smart-youth-work-cervia.costs: Fully funded: international travel refunded up to a fixed budget per person from Morocco; shared room at Mare e Vita Village; three meals a day; accident and liability insurance; all materials.

mitmunc-xix-2027.about:
MITMUNC is MIT's in-person high-school Model UN, now in its 19th session; background guides are already published.

The conference runs 5–7 February 2027 at MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Cambridge, United States. It is open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

See 'Conference Info' on the official site for registration. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: Hosted at MIT; background guides out
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
mitmunc-xix-2027.eligibility: Open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
See 'Conference Info' on the official site for registration.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
mitmunc-xix-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

mlh-fellowship-remote-2027.about:
The MLH Fellowship, run by Major League Hacking (the student hackathon league), is a 12-week remote programme in which small 'pods' of fellows work on real open-source codebases or engineering projects under the guidance of mentors and engineers from partner companies.

Tracks have included Software Engineering (open source), Production Engineering/Site Reliability and Web3 Engineering. Fellows follow an educational curriculum, ship real contributions, build a portfolio and earn a stipend.

Applications are accepted on a rolling basis for upcoming start dates (batches run several times a year). It is open internationally and is a strong option for students who cannot get a traditional internship.
mlh-fellowship-remote-2027.eligibility: Students and early-career developers aged 18+ (check the FAQ for country and work-authorisation details). Some programming experience required.
how_to_apply: Read the tracks and FAQ on the MLH Fellowship site.
Click 'Apply Now' and complete the application (experience, code sample).
Complete the technical interview if invited.
Join your pod at the next start date.
mlh-fellowship-remote-2027.costs: Free; fellows receive a stipend (amount depends on track and location).

model-wto-2027.about:
Model WTO is a week-long simulation of World Trade Organization negotiations, run by students of the University of St. Gallen, held in St. Gallen and Geneva (home of the WTO).

The conference runs 7–14 April 2027 at St. Gallen and Geneva, Switzerland. It is open to university students worldwide (selection by application). Working language: English.

Apply as a participant through 'How to Participate' on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: Rare WTO trade-negotiation simulation, partly in Geneva
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
model-wto-2027.eligibility: Open to university students worldwide (selection by application). Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Apply as a participant through 'How to Participate' on the official site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
model-wto-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

mpiib-international-summer-internship-20.about:
The MPIIB International Summer Internship places students in research groups of the Max Planck Institute for Infection Biology in Berlin (infectious diseases, immunology, microbiology, cell biology) for three months, from 1 September to 30 November 2027. Interns work on a defined project listed on the programme website and are supported by the group's scientists.

The programme explicitly aims at talented students whose access to first-class higher education is limited by financial, regional or societal barriers, and strongly encourages applicants from low- and middle-income countries on the OECD DAC list (which includes Georgia). Interns receive a EUR 1,400 monthly stipend, travel compensation and accommodation near the institute. Selection: pre-selection, online interview, then offer letter.
highlights: Max Planck research project in infection biology
EUR 1,400/month stipend, travel compensation and housing
Designed for students from low- and middle-income countries
mpiib-international-summer-internship-20.eligibility: International bachelor's (at least 4 semesters completed) or master's students enrolled at a university, in biology, medicine, biochemistry, epidemiology or related fields, with a strong record, good English and strong reasons why their access to first-class education is constrained. Must be available 1 Sep – 30 Nov 2027; voluntary internship only (not for credit).
how_to_apply: Browse the MPIIB-ISI project list and choose a project
Write a motivation letter explaining your interest and the barriers you face
Prepare CV and transcripts
Submit the online application by 27 November 2026
Shortlisted candidates get an online interview; final decisions in February 2027
mpiib-international-summer-internship-20.costs: Stipend EUR 1,400 per month, travel compensation and accommodation near the institute provided. No fees.

mun-new-york-summer-2027.about:

The Open Round (28 January 2027) is held at university and high-school sites or online; top scorers sit the Invitational Round (18 March 2027), and the best go on to represent the US and Canada at the International Linguistics Olympiad.

Students register individually or through a school coordinator; the 2027 student and coordinator handbooks are published on the site.

nasa-human-lander-challenge-2027.about:
The Human Lander Challenge supports NASA's Artemis programme by inviting university teams to tackle a real technology gap; the 2027 theme is lunar communications. In Phase 1 teams submit a proposal and two-minute video; up to 12 finalists receive $9,000 each and, in Phase 2, write a technical paper and present to NASA and industry experts at the HuLC Forum in Huntsville (21–24 June 2027). The top three teams share an $18,000 purse.

See the Phase 1 Guidelines and Participation Agreement for eligibility (NASA university challenges usually require teams from accredited US institutions, sometimes allowing international partners).
highlights: Present to NASA experts in Huntsville
nasa-human-lander-challenge-2027.eligibility: Collegiate student teams with a faculty advisor; check the Phase 1 Guidelines for institution and nationality rules.

nasa-space-apps-new-york-2026.about:
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: New York City is the New York City local event of NASA's International Space Apps Challenge, where teams solve NASA-set challenges with open space and Earth data. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at NASA Space Apps local event, Brooklyn in New York from 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-15. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.

nasa-space-apps-new-york-2026.eligibility: Open to anyone who registers for the local event (students, coders, scientists, designers); under-18s need guardian consent under Space Apps rules.

They first compete at school/local and affiliate (state or international) contests in spring; top entries advance to the National Contest at the University of Maryland, College Park on 13–17 June 2027. International schools in China, Korea and elsewhere take part through NHD International.

nawa-polish-language-summer-courses-2027.about:
NAWA, Poland's National Agency for Academic Exchange, funds summer and year-round courses in Polish language and culture at universities with leading centres for teaching Polish as a foreign language. On-site courses last 1–4 weeks and online courses 1–12 weeks; most combine Polish lessons with lectures and workshops on Polish history, culture and everyday life, trips to major sights, integration events and meetings with Polish students, scholars and public figures.

Courses are free of charge: for on-site courses, accommodation and meals are also covered. Participants pay only their travel to and from Poland and compulsory medical insurance (unless their country has an agreement with Poland). Each person may attend only one on-site course per year (plus online options).

For 2027, NAWA will publish dates, course types and host universities at the beginning of December 2026; applications open, in most cases, at the beginning of February 2027 through each university. Summer courses are aimed mainly at international students and academics; check each course for level and eligibility.

Mix of language classes, culture workshops and trips
nawa-polish-language-summer-courses-2027.eligibility: Mainly international students and academic staff (see NAWA eligibility list for summer courses); Georgian applicants can apply. One on-site course per person per year.
